trick: "Run the tests before you finish": does one sentence make it check its work?
source_note: Season 2 lineup (19 Oct, Speed; was day 41 in the 15 Sep plan). With: the prompt starts with the one sentence 'Run the tests before you finish.' and a blank line; without: the task prompt alone. Nothing else differs. The 15 Sep plan had a Bash-logging hook on both sides to count test runs; it is not needed, since every tool call has been saved in raw/<run>.events.jsonl since 15 Sep, so no hook is installed on either side. Standard verdict rule. Pre-registered count (tricks/d46/count_commands.py d46): runs on each side that actually ran a test command (harness/evidence.py's TEST_RE on the Bash calls), and runs whose last test command came after their last edit. Base rate measured 23 Oct with count_commands.py on days 1-30 (Haiku 4.5, all sides): a test command ran in 193 of 193 t2 runs and 169 of 174 h2 runs, but the last test run came after the last edit in only 55 of 174 h2 runs (32%; t2 97%). 'Ran the tests at all' is therefore near its ceiling on these tasks, and 'tests after the last edit' is the part that can move.
tasks_note: Fixed 23 Oct by the E1 pilot (PROTOCOL 2026-10-23 pilot entry): t2 and h2 on Haiku 4.5.
behaviour_count: Runs that ran a test command at least once (from events), with vs without; plus runs whose last test run came after their last edit
